name: SiteSuperCharger
author: AnAdminer

sections.description:
SiteSuperCharger helps your website look as attractive as possible to search engines helping you to acheive the highest search engine rankings.

Contact Marketing Heroes (https://www.mheroes.com) to get started!
sections.installation:
Install SiteSuperCharger via the plugin directory, or by uploading the files manually to your server. After activating SiteSuperCharger, you’ll need to enter your GUID at Settings -> SiteSuperCharger

For info about acquiring a GUID for SiteSuperCharger visit https://www.mheroes.com.
sections.faq:
Is SiteSuperCharger free?

You must purchase Search Engine Optimization services from Marketing Heroes (https://www.mheroes.com) to use SiteSuperCharger
sections.changelog:
5.8.15

  • Fix: the API token you enter on the settings page now saves and stays saved.
  • Fix: a saved token is shown masked so you can confirm the right one is in place.

5.8.14

  • Fix: restores landing pages that were unexpectedly missing after an earlier update.
  • Fix: protects SiteSuperCharger pages from being removed during routine rebuilds.
  • Fix: clears legacy redirects on sites using a third-party SEO redirect tool.

5.8.13

  • Fix: restores landing pages still being redirected to a broken URL by a third-party redirect plugin.
  • Fix: prevents future page renames from creating those broken redirects.

5.8.12

  • Fix: restores landing pages that were redirecting to a broken URL and returning a 404.
  • Fix: prevents the redirect-hijack from happening again on future page updates.

5.8.10

  • Fix: pages with very long content stay reliable on PHP 8.1+ even at the largest body sizes.
  • Fix: sites that previously used a third-party sitemap shortcode now display the full SiteSuperCharger sitemap automatically.

5.8.9

  • Fix: pages with very long content no longer trigger a server error on PHP 8.1+.

5.8.7

  • Fix: robots.txt compatibility with major search engines.
  • Fix: cleans up legacy robots.txt content on first load after update.

5.8.6

  • Fix: prevents duplicate-post creation on large rebuilds.
  • Fix: transient HTTP errors during rebuilds now retry with backoff.
  • Carryforward: includes v5.8.4 and v5.8.5 (held internal, never shipped to wp.org).

5.8.5

  • Fix: canonical-host redirects on subdirectory installs preserve the path. (Bundled into 5.8.6.)

5.8.4

  • Fix: canonical-host enforcement skips .htaccess writes on multisite installs. (Bundled into 5.8.6.)

5.8.3

  • Fix: canonical-host enforcement installs reliably on every plugin update path.

5.8.2

  • Improvement: visitors on the non-canonical host are 301-redirected to the canonical host on every request, consolidating ranking signals.
  • Improvement: bot-crawler policy bundle included (originally held as v5.8.0 / v5.8.1).

5.5.29

Release date: Apr 26th, 2026

  • Improvement: SiteSuperCharger now keeps itself up to date automatically, so your site always runs the latest version without manual updates. This can be turned off if you need to stay on a specific version. Other plugins on your site are unaffected.

5.5.28

Release date: Apr 25th, 2026

  • Improvement: The Overview tab now shows your site’s connection details with click-to-select formatting, making support tickets quicker to file.
  • New: A “Sync now” button on the Overview tab pulls your latest settings from SiteSuperCharger immediately, handy right after you change settings.
  • Improvement: When you publish or update a page or post, that page’s cache is refreshed automatically so visitors see fresh content right away.
  • New: A clear on-screen warning now appears if your site’s connection to SiteSuperCharger needs attention, so you can fix it before features are affected.
  • Improvement: Clearer sitemap status messaging.
  • Improvement: The AI crawler policy setting is now a plain-English option list with a description for each choice, plus a link to view your live robots.txt so you can confirm the policy took effect.
  • New: Lead-conversion tracking for Gravity Forms, Contact Form 7, WPForms, and Formidable Forms: successful form submissions are now recorded as conversions automatically, with no extra plugin required.
  • New: Connect a Cloudflare account directly from the Security tab. Your credentials are sent securely to SiteSuperCharger and are never stored on your WordPress site.
  • Improvement: Sensitive credentials are no longer kept on your WordPress site; SiteSuperCharger performs credential-based actions on your behalf.
  • New: An “Export URLs” option on the Sitemap tab downloads a CSV of every published URL on your site (pages, posts, and public custom post types), replacing the need for a separate export plugin.
  • Improvement: More accurate plugin recommendations, including guidance on which separately installed plugins SiteSuperCharger now makes redundant.
  • Improvement: Refreshed save-button styling across the admin screens.
  • New: A manual “refresh this page’s cache” button on the post and page editor for when you want to clear the cache without re-saving.
  • New: A daily email digest when your site’s overall SiteSuperCharger health grade drops a letter, listing the failing checks. No email on recoveries or unchanged grades; can be turned off in settings.
  • New: A “Recent activity” card on the Overview tab shows the last few things SiteSuperCharger has done, without leaving the page.
  • Improvement: Maintenance actions are now clearer, with a labelled description and button for each.
  • New: A “How to reach a perfect score” guidance bar on the Health tab (shown when your grade is below A) lists the most common gaps in plain language.
  • Improvement: Add redirects directly from the Redirects tab with an inline form, instead of switching to the classic admin screen.
  • Improvement: The Tracking tab now lists every tracking ID your site emits and whether each is configured, so you can see exactly what’s active at a glance.
  • New: A “Current schema values” card on the Schema tab shows how many trust badges and reviews are configured, plus a one-click button to run Google’s Rich Results test for your home page.
  • Fix: Closes a landing-page 404 issue caused by slug collisions. When a landing page’s preferred URL was already taken by another page, SiteSuperCharger used to create the page at a slightly different URL, breaking the canonical link. SiteSuperCharger now reclaims the correct URL safely: any stale or conflicting page is preserved (moved to Trash or renamed, recoverable) so the intended landing-page URL is restored.

5.5.27

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • New: A daily file-integrity check watches your plugin, theme, and core files for unexpected changes, helping catch tampering and silent file corruption early.
  • Improvement: Bundles every fix and feature from 5.5.22 through 5.5.26 (cumulative release).

5.5.26

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • WooCommerce purchase tracking in Google Analytics 4: product views, add-to-cart, checkout-started, and completed purchases all flow into GA4 automatically — no separate plugin needed. Includes a duplicate-event guard so refreshing the thank-you page never inflates revenue numbers.

5.5.25

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • New [ssc-howto] shortcode for service landing pages: produces a step-by-step instruction list with the search-engine schema markup that Google uses for HowTo rich results.
  • Redundant-plugin nudge: when SiteSuperCharger now covers something a separately installed plugin used to do (for example MonsterInsights, Insert Headers and Footers, the Cloudflare official plugin), the admin sees a one-time, dismissible notice on activation pointing them to the SiteSuperCharger setting that replaces it.

5.5.24

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • Spam blog-post quarantine: backlink-spam posts (casino / pharma / payday-loan patterns) are auto-moved to Trash and an email is sent to the admin. Nothing is ever permanently deleted — every action is recoverable from Trash.

5.5.23

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • New: Google Consent Mode v2 support: tracking pixels (Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Google Ads) now start in a privacy-respecting “denied” state and only upgrade to full tracking once the visitor accepts cookies through your consent banner. Works with common consent banners including CookieYes, Complianz, and Cookiebot.
  • Google Ads remarketing / conversion tag: enter a Google Ads ID in tracking settings and the AW- conversion tag is injected automatically.

5.5.22

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • Fix: Closed two account-enumeration leaks that let anonymous visitors harvest usernames and site settings. Logged-in editors and admins still get normal access. Together with the existing protections, this stops the most common username-harvesting probes used against WordPress.
  • Improvement: Admin improvements.

5.5.21

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • New: Delete leftover (orphaned) plugin folders directly from the Plugins tab, with safety checks so only genuine leftovers can be removed.
  • Improvement: Expanded plugin recommendations, flagging plugins that conflict with SiteSuperCharger, that are unnecessary on a managed site, or that SiteSuperCharger already covers.

5.5.20

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • New: The Plugins tab now flags dangerous, conflicting, duplicate, and orphaned plugin installs, with a summary banner and per-row labels so you can see at a glance what needs attention.
  • New: Leftover plugin folders (disabled, old, or backup copies) are detected and surfaced for cleanup.
  • Improvement: The Plugins tab “Updated” column now shows the month and year for clarity across release years.
  • Improvement: Cleaner sitemap display on the Sitemap tab.

5.5.19

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • og:video tags for blog posts with embedded YouTube/Vimeo (og:video, og:video:type, og:video:width/height).
  • preconnect hints for Google Maps on landing pages (maps.googleapis.com + maps.gstatic.com).
  • preconnect hints for YouTube/Vimeo on blog posts with detected video embeds.

5.5.18

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • Twitter/X Card meta tags on all landing pages and blog posts (twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, twitter:image).
  • Blog post Open Graph completeness: og:type=article, og:url, og:locale, og:site_name, article:published_time, article:modified_time, article:author, article:section, og:image:width/height.
  • Landing page og:image:width + og:image:height via WP attachment lookup for richer social previews.
  • AI Crawler Policy settings card in v6 Security tab – editable with live AJAX save and robots.txt sync.

5.5.17

Release date: Apr 22nd, 2026

  • New: Each site now reports its health (plugin/WordPress/PHP versions, content totals, and any plugin conflicts) automatically, so account managers can see site status without logging in.
  • New: Content cross-check catches missing or extra pages, blog posts, and FAQs early.
  • New: Common maintenance tasks (refresh cache, refresh settings, rebuild content) can now be triggered for you without anyone logging into the site.
  • Improvement: Blog post featured images are now described to Google with their dimensions, improving how posts appear in search results and Google Discover.

5.5.16

Release date: Apr 22nd, 2026

  • Speed tab: per-site toggle to turn the built-in HTML minifier on or off. Useful when Cloudflare’s own minify is also active and the two conflict.

5.5.15

Release date: Apr 22nd, 2026

  • Critical fix for the HTML minifier: very large pages could trigger a regex backtrack that produced a blank response (white screen). The minifier now falls back to the unminified page in that situation instead of returning nothing.
  • HTML minifier default changed to OFF on auto-update so existing sites are never silently regressed; admins can opt back in from the Speed tab.

5.5.14

Release date: Apr 22nd, 2026

  • Cloudflare cache purges are now scoped strictly to the www. and apex domain — staging or unrelated subdomains on the same Cloudflare zone are no longer touched.

5.5.0

Release date: Apr 18th, 2026

  • Important security fix: arbitrary HTML / JavaScript can no longer be pushed into a site’s <head> or footer through the admin-app channel. Custom head/footer scripts are still editable in the local plugin settings (gated on manage_options + unfiltered_html capabilities), but the remote-config channel is now restricted to allow-listed IDs (Facebook Pixel, GA4 measurement ID, GTM container ID) that are validated against a strict pattern at injection time. Closes a stored-XSS class of bugs that could have affected every connected site simultaneously if the admin channel had been compromised.
